source.text: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ףאַ֤ךְ ט֭וֹב לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֱלֹהִ֗ים לְבָרֵ֥י לֵבָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: A psalm of Asaph. Surely good to Israel [is] God, to [the] pure of heart.

en.L: A psalm of Asaph. \q Surely God [is] good to Israel, \q to [the] pure of heart.
en.B: A psalm of Asaph. \q God really is good to Israel, \q to people with a clean heart.
en.R: A song of Asaph. \q It is true: God is good to Israel, \q to everyone whose heart is pure.

fr.L: Psaume d’Asaph. \q Assurément, Dieu [est] bon pour Israël, \q pour [ceux qui ont] le cœur pur.
fr.B: Psaume d’Asaph. \q Oui, Dieu est vraiment bon pour Israël, \q pour ceux qui ont le cœur pur.
fr.R: Chant d’Asaph. \q C’est vrai : Dieu est bon pour Israël, \q pour tous ceux qui ont le cœur pur.

sw.L: Zaburi ya Asafu. \q Hakika Mungu [ni] mwema kwa Israeli, \q kwa [wale walio] safi wa moyo.
sw.B: Zaburi ya Asafu. \q Kweli Mungu ni mwema kwa Israeli, \q kwa watu wenye moyo safi.
sw.R: Wimbo wa Asafu. \q Ni kweli: Mungu ni mwema kwa Israeli, \q kwa kila mtu mwenye moyo safi.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the first psalm of Book Three
decisions.reason: Psalm 73 opens the third of the five books of the Psalms (Psalms 73-89), and the group of eleven psalms of Asaph (73-83).

decisions.choice: Asaph: a leader of the temple singers
decisions.reason: Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed to lead the singing before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5-7); his family carried on the work. Psalms 50 and 73-83 bear his name.

decisions.choice: surely: truly, after all
decisions.reason: The word ('akh) affirms something against doubt. It opens the psalm's conclusion before its struggle, and comes back at its turning points (verses 13, 18).

decisions.choice: pure of heart: true and clean within
decisions.reason: As in 24:4: people whose inner life and motives are clean before God.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

decisions.choice: "Psaume d'Asaph" (Literal, Balanced); "Chant d'Asaph" (Readable), for the titles of this block
decisions.reason: Mizmor is "psaume" at Literal and Balanced and "chant" at Readable, as the terms note sets for every psalm. French titles usually go without the article. Asaph keeps his usual French form.

decisions.choice: "Zaburi ya Asafu" (L, B) and "Wimbo wa Asafu" (R) for mizmor, with the singer's name as "Asafu", through Psalms 73-83
decisions.reason: The terms note gives "zaburi" for mizmor and "wimbo" at Readable, where the English says "song"; "Asafu" is the usual Swahili form of the name.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֗י כִּ֭מְעַט נָטָ֣יוּ רַגְלָ֑י כְּ֝אַ֗יִן שֻׁפְּכ֥וּ אֲשֻׁרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: But I — like a little, my feet had turned aside; like nothing, my steps had been poured out.

en.L: But as for me, my feet had almost turned aside; \q my steps had nearly slipped.
en.B: But I came close to losing my footing; \q my steps very nearly slid out from under me.
en.R: But I almost lost my way. \q I very nearly fell away from God.

fr.L: Mais moi, mes pieds avaient presque dévié ; \q mes pas avaient failli glisser.
fr.B: Mais moi, j’ai bien failli perdre pied ; \q mes pas ont presque glissé sous moi.
fr.R: Mais moi, j’ai presque perdu mon chemin. \q J’ai bien failli m’éloigner de Dieu.

sw.L: Lakini mimi, miguu yangu ilikuwa karibu kupotoka; \q hatua zangu zilikuwa karibu kuteleza.
sw.B: Lakini mimi nilikaribia kupoteza mahali pa kukanyaga; \q hatua zangu zilikaribia kabisa kuteleza.
sw.R: Lakini mimi karibu nipotee njia. \q Karibu kabisa nimwache Mungu.

decisions.choice: the words as read, not as written
decisions.reason: Both verbs are marked to be read in a different form from the one written; the sense is the same, "turned aside" and "slipped".

decisions.choice: my feet had almost slipped: I nearly lost my faith
decisions.reason: The picture is of losing one's footing on a path (17:5; 38:17). Here it is his trust in God's goodness (verse 1) that nearly gave way.

decisions.choice: I almost lost my way; I nearly fell away from God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

source.text: כִּֽי־קִ֭נֵּאתִי בַּֽהוֹלְלִ֑ים שְׁל֖וֹם רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֶרְאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For I was jealous of the boastful; [the] peace of [the] wicked I saw.

en.L: For I was jealous of the boastful; \q I saw [the] peace of [the] wicked.
en.B: I had grown jealous of the proud, \q watching wicked people do well.
en.R: I was jealous of proud people. \q I saw that evil people have an easy life.

fr.L: Car j’ai été jaloux des orgueilleux ; \q j’ai vu [la] paix des méchants.
fr.B: J’étais devenu jaloux des arrogants, \q en voyant les méchants réussir.
fr.R: J’étais jaloux des gens orgueilleux. \q Je voyais que les méchants ont la vie facile.

sw.L: Kwa maana niliwaonea wivu wenye kujivuna; \q niliiona amani ya waovu.
sw.B: Nilikuwa nimewaonea wivu wenye kiburi, \q nikiwatazama waovu wakifanikiwa.
sw.R: Niliwaonea wivu watu wenye kiburi. \q Niliona kwamba watu waovu wana maisha rahisi.

decisions.choice: the boastful: the arrogant
decisions.reason: The word (holelim) is those who boast, as in 5:6 and 75:5.

decisions.choice: peace: well-being, success
decisions.reason: The word (shalom) here is the ease and success of the wicked, all going well for them.

decisions.choice: Psalm 37:1
decisions.reason: Psalm 37:1 warns against this envy: "Do not be jealous of those who do wrong".

decisions.choice: "waovu" for the wicked (resha'im) at every level, through Psalms 69-83, with "wenye haki" for the righteous and "wanyofu" for the upright
decisions.reason: These are the words of the terms note. "Waovu" are people whose way of life is evil, which is the sense of the Hebrew word, not people who have done one wrong.

source.text: כִּ֤י אֵ֖ין חַרְצֻבּ֥וֹת לְמוֹתָ֗ם וּבָרִ֥יא אוּלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For there are no pains at their death, and fat [is] their body.

en.L: For there are no pains at their death, \q and their body [is] fat.
en.B: They die without pain, \q and their bodies are plump and healthy.
en.R: They do not suffer, even when they die. \q Their bodies are healthy and well fed.

fr.L: Car il n’y a pas de douleurs à leur mort, \q et leur corps [est] gras.
fr.B: Ils meurent sans souffrance, \q et leur corps est gras et bien portant.
fr.R: Ils ne souffrent pas, même quand ils meurent. \q Leur corps est en bonne santé et bien nourri.

sw.L: Kwa maana hawana maumivu katika kufa kwao, \q na mwili wao [ni] mnono.
sw.B: Hufa bila maumivu, \q na miili yao ni minono na yenye afya.
sw.R: Hawateseki, hata wanapokufa. \q Miili yao ina afya na wanakula vizuri.

decisions.choice: no pains at their death
alternatives: they have no pains; their body is sound and fat (dividing the words differently)
decisions.reason: The letters can also be divided to read "they have no pains; sound and fat is their body", which keeps the verse on their life rather than their death. The text as divided speaks of an easy death.

decisions.choice: fat: well fed
decisions.reason: Being fat was a sign of plenty and health (92:15), not a fault.

source.text: בַּעֲמַ֣ל אֱנ֣וֹשׁ אֵינֵ֑מוֹ וְעִם־אָ֝דָ֗ם לֹ֣א יְנֻגָּֽעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] trouble of man they are not, and with mankind they are not struck.

en.L: They are not in the trouble of [other] people, \q and with [other] people they are not struck.
en.B: They are free from the hardships others carry; \q they are not plagued like the rest of humankind.
en.R: They do not have the troubles other people have. \q They do not suffer like everyone else.

fr.L: Ils ne sont pas dans la peine des [autres] humains, \q et avec les humains ils ne sont pas frappés.
fr.B: Ils ne connaissent pas les peines que portent les autres ; \q ils ne sont pas frappés comme le reste des humains.
fr.R: Ils n’ont pas les ennuis des autres. \q Ils ne souffrent pas comme tout le monde.

sw.L: Hawamo katika taabu ya wanadamu [wengine], \q wala hawapigwi pamoja na watu [wengine].
sw.B: Hawana taabu wanazobeba wengine; \q hawapigwi kama wanadamu wengine.
sw.R: Hawana shida walizo nazo watu wengine. \q Hawateseki kama watu wengine wote.

decisions.choice: man, mankind: ordinary people
decisions.reason: The two words ('enosh, 'adam) both mean human beings: the wicked seem to escape the common lot of mortals.

decisions.choice: struck: struck by trouble or sickness
decisions.reason: The verb (naga') is used of being struck by disease or by God's hand; verse 14 uses it of the speaker himself.

source.text: לָ֭כֵן עֲנָקַ֣תְמוֹ גַאֲוָ֑ה יַעֲטָף־שִׁ֝֗ית חָמָ֥ס לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore pride [is] their necklace; a garment of violence covers them.

en.L: Therefore pride [is] their necklace; \q a garment of violence covers them.
en.B: So they wear pride like a chain around the neck, \q and violence wraps them like a robe.
en.R: So they show off their pride like a necklace. \q They wear violence like clothes.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi l’orgueil [est] leur collier ; \q un vêtement de violence les couvre.
fr.B: Alors ils portent l’orgueil comme une chaîne autour du cou, \q et la violence les enveloppe comme un manteau.
fr.R: Alors ils montrent leur orgueil comme un collier. \q Ils portent la violence comme des habits.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo kiburi [ni] mkufu wao shingoni; \q vazi la jeuri linawafunika.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo huvaa kiburi kama mkufu shingoni, \q na jeuri huwafunika kama joho.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo huonyesha kiburi chao kama mkufu. \q Huvaa jeuri kama nguo.

decisions.choice: pride a necklace, violence a garment: worn openly
decisions.reason: They display their pride and their violence as proudly as jewelry and fine clothes, for all to see.

source.text: יָ֭צָא מֵחֵ֣לֶב עֵינֵ֑מוֹ עָ֝בְר֗וּ מַשְׂכִּיּ֥וֹת לֵבָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: It goes out from fat, their eye; they pass over, [the] imaginations of [the] heart.

en.L: Their eye bulges out from fat; \q the imaginations of [their] heart overflow.
en.B: Their eyes bulge from their fat faces; \q the fancies of their minds run past all limits.
en.R: They are so fat that their eyes bulge. \q Their heads are full of foolish plans.

fr.L: Leur œil sort de la graisse ; \q les imaginations du cœur débordent.
fr.B: Leurs yeux sortent de leur visage gras ; \q les rêveries de leur esprit dépassent toute mesure.
fr.R: Ils sont si gros que leurs yeux sortent de la tête. \q Leur tête est pleine de projets insensés.

sw.L: Jicho lao hutoka nje kwa unono; \q mawazo ya [mioyo yao] hufurika.
sw.B: Macho yao hutokeza katika nyuso zao nono; \q mawazo ya akili zao hupita mipaka yote.
sw.R: Wamenenepa mno hata macho yao yametokeza. \q Vichwa vyao vimejaa mipango ya kipumbavu.

decisions.choice: their eye
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation read a word with almost the same letters, "their wrongdoing comes out from fat", that is, from hearts dulled by plenty (17:10).

decisions.choice: imaginations: what their minds dream up
decisions.reason: The word (maskiyyot) is something imagined or pictured; their pride and plans know no limit.

source.text: יָמִ֤יקוּ׀וִידַבְּר֣וּ בְרָ֣ע עֹ֑שֶׁק מִמָּר֥וֹם יְדַבֵּֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: They mock and they speak with evil [of] oppression; from on high they speak.

en.L: They mock and speak with evil [of] oppression; \q from on high they speak.
en.B: They jeer and talk of evil; \q from on high they speak of crushing others.
en.R: They make fun of others and say cruel things. \q They act as if they were above everyone, and they threaten to hurt people.

fr.L: Ils raillent et parlent avec méchanceté [d’]oppression ; \q de haut ils parlent.
fr.B: Ils ricanent et parlent de faire le mal ; \q de haut, ils parlent d’écraser les autres.
fr.R: Ils se moquent des autres et disent des choses cruelles. \q Ils se croient au-dessus de tout le monde et menacent de faire du mal aux gens.

sw.L: Hudhihaki na kunena kwa ubaya [juu ya] dhuluma; \q hunena kutoka juu.
sw.B: Hudhihaki na kuzungumza mabaya; \q kutoka juu hunena juu ya kuwakandamiza wengine.
sw.R: Huwacheka wengine na kusema maneno ya ukatili. \q Hujifanya wako juu ya kila mtu, na hutisha kuwadhuru watu.

decisions.choice: speak with evil of oppression
alternatives: speak with evil; they speak of oppression from on high
decisions.reason: The word "oppression" can go with the first half or the second; the meaning is much the same: they talk of crushing others.

decisions.choice: from on high: from a lofty height, looking down on others
decisions.reason: They speak as if they sat above everyone, even with God's authority (verse 9).

source.text: שַׁתּ֣וּ בַשָּׁמַ֣יִם פִּיהֶ֑ם וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם תִּֽהֲלַ֥ךְ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: They set in the heavens their mouth, and their tongue walks in the earth.

en.L: They set their mouth in the heavens, \q and their tongue walks through the earth.
en.B: Their mouths speak as if they owned heaven; \q their tongues go swaggering through the land.
en.R: They talk as if they ruled heaven. \q They say whatever they like about everything on earth.

fr.L: Ils mettent leur bouche dans les cieux, \q et leur langue se promène sur la terre.
fr.B: Leur bouche parle comme si le ciel leur appartenait ; \q leur langue se pavane à travers le pays.
fr.R: Ils parlent comme s’ils régnaient sur le ciel. \q Ils disent ce qu’ils veulent sur tout ce qui est sur la terre.

sw.L: Huweka kinywa chao mbinguni, \q na ulimi wao hutembea katika dunia.
sw.B: Vinywa vyao husema kana kwamba mbingu ni mali yao; \q ndimi zao hutamba katika nchi.
sw.R: Huzungumza kana kwamba wanatawala mbinguni. \q Husema lolote wanalotaka juu ya kila kitu duniani.

decisions.choice: set their mouth in the heavens: speak as if they ruled heaven and earth
alternatives: set their mouth against the heavens
decisions.reason: Their talk reaches up to heaven and over all the earth: they speak against God and lord it over people.

source.text: לָכֵ֤ן׀יָשׁ֣וּב עַמּ֣וֹ הֲלֹ֑ם וּמֵ֥י מָ֝לֵ֗א יִמָּ֥צוּ לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore his people turn back here, and waters of fullness are drained by them.

en.L: Therefore {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people turn back here, \q and waters of fullness are drained by them.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people turn their way \q and gulp down their words like water from a full cup.
en.R: So even God's people turn to follow them. \q They take in everything those people say, as if they were drinking water.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple se tourne par ici, \q et des eaux en abondance sont bues par eux.
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple se tourne vers eux \q et boit leurs paroles comme l’eau d’une coupe pleine.
fr.R: Alors même le peuple de Dieu se met à les suivre. \q Il avale tout ce que disent ces gens, comme on boit de l’eau.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hugeukia huku, \q na maji ya kujaa hunywewa nao.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} huwageukia \q na kuyanywa maneno yao kama maji ya kikombe kilichojaa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hata watu wa Mungu huwageukia na kuwafuata. \q Hupokea kila kitu wanachosema watu hao, kana kwamba wanakunywa maji.

decisions.choice: turn back: the word as read, not as written
alternatives: he brings his people back here (as written)
decisions.reason: The word is written as "he brings back" and marked to be read as "they turn back". The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: his people turn here and drink: people are drawn to the wicked
alternatives: God's people turn back to this question
decisions.reason: The verse is one of the hardest in the psalm. "His people" is most likely God's people, who turn to the wicked and take in their talk as freely as water. Others read it of the wicked man's followers.

decisions.choice: God's people
decisions.reason: Readable names whose people are meant, following the likeliest reading (m2).

source.text: וְֽאָמְר֗וּ אֵיכָ֥ה יָדַֽע־אֵ֑ל וְיֵ֖שׁ דֵּעָ֣ה בְעֶלְיֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they say, How does God know? And is there knowledge with [the] Most High?

en.L: And they say, "How does God know? \q And is there knowledge with [the] Most High?"
en.B: And they ask, "What can God know? \q Is the Most High aware of anything?"
en.R: They say, "God cannot know what we do. \q The God who is above all does not see it."

fr.L: Et ils disent : « Comment Dieu saurait-il ? \q Et y a-t-il de la connaissance chez [le] Très-Haut ? »
fr.B: Et ils demandent : « Que peut savoir Dieu ? \q Le Très-Haut se rend-il compte de quelque chose ? »
fr.R: Ils disent : « Dieu ne peut pas savoir ce que nous faisons. \q Le Dieu qui est au-dessus de tout ne le voit pas. »

sw.L: Nao husema, "Mungu anajuaje? \q Je, kuna maarifa kwa Aliye Juu?"
sw.B: Nao huuliza, "Mungu anaweza kujua nini? \q Je, Aliye Juu anafahamu jambo lolote?"
sw.R: Husema, "Mungu hawezi kujua tunayofanya. \q Mungu aliye juu ya wote haoni."

decisions.choice: how does God know: God does not notice
decisions.reason: The question is a scoffing denial, as in 10:11 and 94:7: the wicked act as if God does not see or care.

decisions.choice: the Most High: God above all
decisions.reason: As in 46:5.

decisions.choice: statements
alternatives: How does God know? Is there knowledge with the Most High?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the scoffing questions into the claims they make (m1), and says "the God who is above all" for "the Most High".

source.text: הִנֵּה־אֵ֥לֶּה רְשָׁעִ֑ים וְשַׁלְוֵ֥י ע֝וֹלָ֗ם הִשְׂגּוּ־חָֽיִל׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, these [are the] wicked, and always at ease they have increased wealth.

en.L: Look, these [are the] wicked, \q and always at ease they have increased [in] wealth.
en.B: So these are the wicked: \q never troubled, always growing richer.
en.R: Look at these evil people! \q They never have a care, and they keep getting richer.

fr.L: Voici, ceux-là [sont des] méchants, \q et toujours tranquilles, ils ont accru [leur] richesse.
fr.B: Voilà donc les méchants : \q jamais inquiets, toujours plus riches.
fr.R: Regarde ces méchants ! \q Ils n’ont jamais de souci, et ils deviennent toujours plus riches.

sw.L: Tazama, hawa [ndio] waovu, \q na daima wakiwa na raha wameongezeka [katika] mali.
sw.B: Ndivyo walivyo waovu: \q hawasumbuki kamwe, huzidi kutajirika daima.
sw.R: Watazame watu hawa waovu! \q Hawana wasiwasi wowote, nao huzidi kutajirika.

decisions.choice: always at ease: untroubled for ever
decisions.reason: The word (shalev) is the quiet ease of those with nothing to fear.

source.text: אַךְ־רִ֭יק זִכִּ֣יתִי לְבָבִ֑י וָאֶרְחַ֖ץ בְּנִקָּי֣וֹן כַּפָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Surely in vain I have kept pure my heart and washed in innocence my hands.

en.L: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure \q and washed my hands in innocence.
en.B: So it was for nothing that I kept my heart clean \q and washed my hands to show I was innocent.
en.R: It seemed useless for me to keep my heart pure \q and to stay away from doing wrong.

fr.L: Assurément, c’est en vain que j’ai gardé mon cœur pur \q et lavé mes mains dans l’innocence.
fr.B: C’est donc pour rien que j’ai gardé mon cœur net \q et que je me suis lavé les mains pour montrer mon innocence.
fr.R: Cela me semblait inutile de garder mon cœur pur \q et de ne pas faire le mal.

sw.L: Hakika bure nimeutakasa moyo wangu \q na kunawa mikono yangu katika kutokuwa na hatia.
sw.B: Kumbe ilikuwa bure kwamba niliweka moyo wangu safi \q na kunawa mikono yangu kuonyesha kwamba sina hatia.
sw.R: Ilionekana kazi bure kwangu kuuweka moyo wangu safi \q na kukaa mbali na kutenda mabaya.

decisions.choice: surely in vain: what he thought then
decisions.reason: Verses 13-14 give the bitter thought he had before he went into God's sanctuary (verse 17). "Surely" ('akh) answers the "surely" of verse 1.

decisions.choice: washed my hands in innocence: kept myself free of guilt
decisions.reason: Washing the hands was a sign of innocence (26:6; Deuteronomy 21:6-7).

decisions.choice: stay away from doing wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

source.text: וָאֱהִ֣י נָ֭גוּעַ כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם וְ֝תוֹכַחְתִּ֗י לַבְּקָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I have been struck all the day, and my rebuke [was] every morning.

en.L: For I have been struck all the day, \q and my punishment [came] every morning.
en.B: I have been beaten down the whole day long, \q and corrected afresh each morning.
en.R: I suffer all day long. \q Every morning I am punished again.

fr.L: Car j’ai été frappé tout le jour, \q et ma punition [venait] chaque matin.
fr.B: J’ai été accablé tout au long du jour, \q et corrigé de nouveau chaque matin.
fr.R: Je souffre toute la journée. \q Chaque matin, je suis puni encore.

sw.L: Kwa maana nimepigwa mchana kutwa, \q na adhabu yangu [ilikuja] kila asubuhi.
sw.B: Nimepigwa chini mchana kutwa, \q na kurudiwa upya kila asubuhi.
sw.R: Ninateseka mchana kutwa. \q Kila asubuhi ninaadhibiwa tena.

decisions.choice: rebuke: correction, punishment
decisions.reason: The word (tokechah) is a rebuke or correction; his suffering felt like God's punishment though he had kept himself pure.

decisions.choice: every morning: day after day
decisions.reason: "To the mornings" means each morning, again and again.

source.text: אִם־אָ֭מַרְתִּי אֲסַפְּרָ֥ה כְמ֑וֹ הִנֵּ֤ה ד֭וֹר בָּנֶ֣יךָ בָגָֽדְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: If I had said, I will speak thus, look, [the] generation of your children I would have betrayed.

en.L: If I had said I would speak like this, \q look, I would have betrayed the generation of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} children.
en.B: Had I resolved to speak like this, \q I would have broken faith with the family of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} children.
en.R: If I had told others what I was thinking, \q I would have let down all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.

fr.L: Si j’avais dit que je parlerais ainsi, \q voici, j’aurais trahi la génération de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} enfants.
fr.B: Si j’avais décidé de parler ainsi, \q j’aurais trahi la famille de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} enfants.
fr.R: Si j’avais dit aux autres ce que je pensais, \q j’aurais fait du tort à tout {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple.

sw.L: Kama ningalisema ningenena hivi, \q tazama, ningalikisaliti kizazi cha watoto {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.B: Kama ningaliamua kusema hivi, \q ningalivunja uaminifu kwa jamaa ya watoto {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.R: Kama ningaliwaambia wengine niliyokuwa nikiwaza, \q ningaliwaangusha watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wote.

decisions.choice: the generation of your children: God's people
decisions.reason: The "children" are God's children, the community of those who belong to him (Deuteronomy 14:1); "generation" is the circle of the faithful (14:5; 24:6).

decisions.choice: betrayed: been false to
decisions.reason: The verb (bagad) is to break faith. To voice his doubts as truth would have been to abandon his fellow believers.

decisions.choice: told others what I was thinking
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that "like this" refers to the thoughts of verses 13-14.

source.text: וָֽ֭אֲחַשְּׁבָה לָדַ֣עַת זֹ֑את עָמָ֖ל ה֣וּא בְעֵינָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I thought to understand this; trouble it [was] in my eyes,

en.L: And I thought [how] to understand this; \q it [was] trouble in my eyes,
en.B: So I tried to make sense of it, \q but it seemed a weary task to me,
en.R: I tried to understand all this. \q But it was too hard for me.

fr.L: Et j’ai réfléchi [pour] comprendre cela ; \q c’[était] une peine à mes yeux,
fr.B: Alors j’ai cherché à comprendre cela, \q mais la tâche m’a paru pénible,
fr.R: J’ai essayé de comprendre tout cela. \q Mais c’était trop difficile pour moi.

sw.L: Nami nikawaza [jinsi ya] kuelewa jambo hili; \q [likawa] taabu machoni pangu,
sw.B: Basi nilijaribu kulielewa jambo hilo, \q lakini lilionekana kazi ya kuchosha kwangu,
sw.R: Nilijaribu kuelewa mambo haya yote. \q Lakini yalikuwa magumu mno kwangu.

decisions.choice: it: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The written and read forms differ only in spelling; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: "Until" in verse 17 finishes the thought, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: עַד־אָ֭בוֹא אֶל־מִקְדְּשֵׁי־אֵ֑ל אָ֝בִ֗ינָה לְאַחֲרִיתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: until I came into [the] sanctuaries of God; I understood their end.

en.L: until I went into the sanctuary of God; \q [then] I understood their end.
en.B: until I entered God's holy place; \q then I saw where they will end.
en.R: Then I went into God's temple. \q There I understood what will happen to them in the end.

fr.L: jusqu’à ce que je vienne dans le sanctuaire de Dieu ; \q [alors] j’ai compris leur fin.
fr.B: jusqu’au jour où je suis entré dans le lieu saint de Dieu ; \q alors j’ai vu où ils finiront.
fr.R: Puis je suis allé dans le temple de Dieu. \q Là, j’ai compris ce qui leur arrivera à la fin.

sw.L: mpaka nilipoingia patakatifu pa Mungu; \q [ndipo] nilipoufahamu mwisho wao.
sw.B: mpaka nilipoingia mahali patakatifu pa Mungu; \q ndipo nikaona watakavyoishia.
sw.R: Kisha nikaingia katika hekalu la Mungu. \q Huko nikaelewa yatakayowapata mwishoni.

decisions.choice: the sanctuaries of God: God's holy place
decisions.reason: The plural may mean the temple and its courts, or be a plural of majesty for the one sanctuary (68:36). There, in God's presence, the speaker sees things as they are.

decisions.choice: their end: what finally becomes of them
decisions.reason: The word ('acharit) is the end or outcome, the last part of the story (37:37-38).

decisions.choice: the turning point of the psalm
decisions.reason: Worship changes his view: verses 18-28 answer verses 2-16.

source.text: אַ֣ךְ בַּ֭חֲלָקוֹת תָּשִׁ֣ית לָ֑מוֹ הִ֝פַּלְתָּ֗ם לְמַשּׁוּאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Surely on slippery [places] you set them; you make them fall to ruins.

en.L: Surely on slippery [places] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set them; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make them fall to ruin.
en.B: In fact, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set them where the footing is slick, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} let them crash into ruin.
en.R: You have put them in a place where they can easily slip. \q You make them fall and be destroyed.

fr.L: Assurément, sur des [lieux] glissants {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les places ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les fais tomber en ruines.
fr.B: Oui, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as placés sur un sol glissant, \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les laisses s’effondrer dans la ruine.
fr.R: Tu les as mis dans un endroit où ils peuvent glisser facilement. \q Tu les fais tomber et ils sont détruits.

sw.L: Hakika {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} huwaweka mahali penye utelezi; \q {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} huwaangusha kwenye uharibifu.
sw.B: Kwa kweli {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umewaweka mahali penye utelezi, \q nawe unawaacha waanguke na kuangamia.
sw.R: Umewaweka mahali ambapo wanaweza kuteleza kwa urahisi. \q Unawaangusha, nao wanaangamizwa.

decisions.choice: slippery places: the answer to verse 2
decisions.reason: He thought his own feet were slipping (verse 2); now he sees that it is the wicked who stand on slippery ground (35:6).

decisions.choice: ruins: destruction
decisions.reason: The word (mashshu'ot) is found only here and in 74:3. It probably means ruins; a similar word means deceptions.

source.text: אֵ֤יךְ הָי֣וּ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה כְרָ֑גַע סָ֥פוּ תַ֝֗מּוּ מִן־בַּלָּהֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: How they have become a desolation in a moment! They have come to an end; they are finished from terrors.

en.L: How they have become a desolation in a moment! \q They have come to an end, they are finished by terrors.
en.B: In an instant they are ruined! \q Sudden terrors make an end of them.
en.R: In a moment they are destroyed! \q Terrible things happen to them, and they are gone.

fr.L: Comme ils sont devenus une désolation en un instant ! \q Ils ont pris fin, ils sont achevés par les terreurs.
fr.B: En un instant les voilà ruinés ! \q Des terreurs soudaines les font disparaître.
fr.R: En un moment, ils sont détruits ! \q Des choses terribles leur arrivent, et ils ne sont plus là.

sw.L: Jinsi walivyokuwa ukiwa ghafla! \q Wamekoma, wamekwisha kwa vitisho.
sw.B: Kwa muda mfupi wameangamia! \q Vitisho vya ghafla vinawamaliza.
sw.R: Kwa muda mfupi wameangamizwa! \q Mambo ya kutisha yanawapata, nao wanatoweka.

decisions.choice: terrors: sudden dread and death
decisions.reason: The word (ballahot) is used of the terrors of death and disaster (Job 18:11, 14).

source.text: כַּחֲל֥וֹם מֵהָקִ֑יץ אֲ֝דֹנָי בָּעִ֤יר׀צַלְמָ֬ם תִּבְזֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Like a dream after waking, Lord, when [you] rouse [yourself], their image you will despise.

en.L: Like a dream after waking, \q my Lord, when [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] rouse [{{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}], {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will despise their image.
en.B: They are like a dream once the sleeper wakes; \q Lord, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stir, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will scorn them as mere shadows.
en.R: They are like a dream that is gone when a person wakes up. \q Lord, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} get up to act, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will treat them as if they were nothing.

fr.L: Comme un rêve après le réveil, \q mon Seigneur, quand [{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}] {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} réveilles, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} méprises leur image.
fr.B: Ils sont comme un rêve quand le dormeur s’éveille ; \q Seigneur, quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} lèveras, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les mépriseras comme de simples ombres.
fr.R: Ils sont comme un rêve qui disparaît quand on se réveille. \q Seigneur, quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} lèveras pour agir, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les traiteras comme s’ils n’étaient rien.

sw.L: Kama ndoto baada ya kuamka, \q Bwana wangu, [{{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}] uamkapo, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utaidharau sura yao.
sw.B: Wao ni kama ndoto mtu anapoamka; \q Bwana, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unapoinuka, utawadharau kama vivuli tu.
sw.R: Wao ni kama ndoto inayotoweka mtu anapoamka. \q Bwana, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unapoinuka kutenda, utawahesabu kuwa si kitu.

decisions.choice: their image: their shadowy form
decisions.reason: The word (tselem) is an image or likeness; here, a shadow without substance (39:7). Like a dream, the success of the wicked vanishes when God acts.

decisions.choice: when you rouse yourself: when God acts
decisions.reason: God seems to sleep while evil goes on and "wakes" when he steps in (44:24). The same letters can be read "in the city".

decisions.choice: my Lord (L); Lord (B, R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, 'Adonai in address is "my Lord" at Literal and "Lord" at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: כִּ֭י יִתְחַמֵּ֣ץ לְבָבִ֑י וְ֝כִלְיוֹתַ֗י אֶשְׁתּוֹנָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: When my heart was embittered and [in] my kidneys I was pierced,

en.L: When my heart was embittered, \q and I was pierced in my kidneys,
en.B: When my heart had turned sour \q and I felt stabbed deep inside,
en.R: My heart was bitter, \q and I was hurt deep inside.

fr.L: Quand mon cœur s’aigrissait, \q et que j’étais transpercé dans mes reins,
fr.B: Quand mon cœur était devenu amer \q et que je me sentais blessé au plus profond de moi,
fr.R: Mon cœur était plein d’amertume, \q et j’étais blessé au fond de moi.

sw.L: Moyo wangu ulipoingiwa na uchungu, \q nami nikachomwa katika figo zangu,
sw.B: Moyo wangu ulipojaa uchungu \q nami nikajisikia kuchomwa ndani kabisa,
sw.R: Moyo wangu ulikuwa na uchungu, \q nami niliumia ndani kabisa.

decisions.choice: kidneys: the inner self, the feelings
decisions.reason: The kidneys were thought of as the seat of the deepest feelings (7:10; 16:7).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The "when" clause is completed in verse 22, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: deep inside
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the picture (m1); Balanced does too.

source.text: וַאֲנִי־בַ֭עַר וְלֹ֣א אֵדָ֑ע בְּ֝הֵמ֗וֹת הָיִ֥יתִי עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: and I [was] stupid and did not know; [like] beasts I was with you.

en.L: then I [was] stupid and did not know; \q [like] a beast I was before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: I was a fool and knew nothing; \q in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence I was no better than an animal.
en.R: I was foolish and did not understand. \q I acted like an animal that cannot think, right in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

fr.L: alors moi, [j’étais] stupide et je ne savais pas ; \q j’étais [comme] une bête devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.
fr.B: j’étais un sot, je ne savais rien ; \q devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, je ne valais pas mieux qu’une bête.
fr.R: J’étais bête et je ne comprenais pas. \q Je me conduisais comme un animal qui ne réfléchit pas, juste devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.

sw.L: ndipo mimi [nilikuwa] mjinga wala sikujua; \q [kama] mnyama nilikuwa mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.B: Nilikuwa mpumbavu nisiyejua kitu; \q mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} sikuwa bora kuliko mnyama.
sw.R: Nilikuwa mpumbavu na sikuelewa. \q Nilitenda kama mnyama asiyeweza kufikiri, mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kabisa.

decisions.choice: beasts: a dumb animal
decisions.reason: The plural (behemot) can mean one large beast (Job 40:15). He confesses that in his bitterness he was as senseless as an animal.

decisions.choice: like
decisions.reason: "A beast I was" is a comparison; the levels say "like" or "no better than".

source.text: וַאֲנִ֣י תָמִ֣יד עִמָּ֑ךְ אָ֝חַ֗זְתָּ בְּיַד־יְמִינִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I [am] continually with you; you hold [me by] my right hand.

en.L: Yet I [am] continually with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have held my right hand.
en.B: Even so, I am with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at all times; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have taken me by the right hand.
en.R: But I am always close to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You hold me by the hand.

fr.L: Pourtant moi, [je suis] continuellement avec {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as tenu ma main droite.
fr.B: Malgré tout, je suis toujours avec {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as pris par la main droite.
fr.R: Mais je suis toujours près de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. \q Tu me tiens par la main.

sw.L: Lakini mimi [niko] pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} daima; \q {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umeushika mkono wangu wa kuume.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, niko pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} siku zote; \q {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umenishika mkono wa kuume.
sw.R: Lakini mimi niko karibu {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} daima. \q Wewe unanishika mkono.

decisions.choice: continually with you: God stayed with him
decisions.reason: Even when he was senseless (verse 22), God did not let him go. The faith of verse 1 returns, now tested.

decisions.choice: you hold my right hand: you lead and keep me
decisions.reason: As a parent or a king takes someone by the hand (Isaiah 41:13; 42:6).

source.text: בַּעֲצָתְךָ֥ תַנְחֵ֑נִי וְ֝אַחַ֗ר כָּב֥וֹד תִּקָּחֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: With your counsel you will guide me, and after, [to] glory you will take me.

en.L: With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} counsel {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} guide me, \q and afterward {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will take me [to] glory.
en.B: You lead me by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wise advice, \q and at the end {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will take me up in glory.
en.R: You guide me by showing me what is wise. \q And at the end {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will take me to be with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in glory.

fr.L: Par {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} conseil {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me conduis, \q et ensuite {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me prendras [dans la] gloire.
fr.B: Tu me guides par {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} sages conseils, \q et à la fin {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me prendras dans la gloire.
fr.R: Tu me guides en me montrant ce qui est sage. \q Et à la fin, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me prendras pour que je sois avec {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} dans la gloire.

sw.L: Kwa shauri {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utaniongoza, \q na baadaye {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utanichukua [kwenye] utukufu.
sw.B: Unaniongoza kwa mashauri {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ya hekima, \q na mwishowe {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utanichukua katika utukufu.
sw.R: Unaniongoza kwa kunionyesha yaliyo ya hekima. \q Na mwishowe {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utanichukua niwe pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} katika utukufu.

decisions.choice: afterward you will take me to glory: beyond this life
alternatives: afterward you will receive me with honor
you will lead me after glory
decisions.reason: "Take" (laqach) is the word used when God took Enoch (Genesis 5:24) and Elijah (2 Kings 2:3, 5), and in 49:16, "God will ransom my life from Sheol, for he will take me". Set against the sudden end of the wicked (verses 18-19), it points to life with God after death, though it may mean honor in this life.

decisions.choice: to be with you
decisions.reason: Readable says where God will take him, following the likeliest sense (m1).

source.text: מִי־לִ֥י בַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְ֝עִמְּךָ֗ לֹא־חָפַ֥צְתִּי בָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Who [is] for me in the heavens? And with you I do not delight in [anything] on the earth.

en.L: Who [is there] for me in the heavens? \q And with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I desire nothing on the earth.
en.B: Who else is there for me in heaven? \q And having {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I want nothing on earth.
en.R: In heaven I have no one but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q And since I have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, there is nothing on earth I want.

fr.L: Qui [ai-je] pour moi dans les cieux ? \q Et avec {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, je ne désire rien sur la terre.
fr.B: Qui d’autre ai-je dans le ciel ? \q Et puisque je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai, je ne veux rien sur la terre.
fr.R: Dans le ciel, je n’ai personne d’autre que {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. \q Et puisque je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai, il n’y a rien sur la terre que je veuille.

sw.L: Ni nani [aliye] kwa ajili yangu mbinguni? \q Na pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} sitamani kitu duniani.
sw.B: Ni nani mwingine niliye naye mbinguni? \q Na kwa kuwa nina {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, sitaki kitu duniani.
sw.R: Mbinguni sina mwingine ila {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}. \q Na kwa kuwa nina {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, hakuna kitu duniani ninachokitaka.

decisions.choice: who is for me in heaven: no one but you
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one but you"; with God, nothing on earth is worth wanting.

decisions.choice: with you: having you, besides you
decisions.reason: The word ('im) is "with": being with God, he wants nothing else.

decisions.choice: I have no one but you
alternatives: Who is there for me in heaven?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects (m1).

source.text: כָּלָ֥ה שְׁאֵרִ֗י וּלְבָ֫בִ֥י צוּר־לְבָבִ֥י וְחֶלְקִ֗י אֱלֹהִ֥ים לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: It has failed, my flesh and my heart; [the] rock of my heart and my portion [is] God forever.

en.L: My flesh and my heart have failed; \q [the] rock of my heart and my portion [is] God forever.
en.B: Though body and heart wear out, \q God is the rock my heart rests on and the share that is mine forever.
en.R: My body and my mind may grow weak. \q But God is like a rock that holds up my heart. He is all I need forever.

fr.L: Ma chair et mon cœur ont défailli ; \q [le] rocher de mon cœur et ma part, [c’est] Dieu pour toujours.
fr.B: Même si mon corps et mon cœur s’épuisent, \q Dieu est le rocher où mon cœur s’appuie et la part qui est à moi pour toujours.
fr.R: Mon corps et mon esprit peuvent devenir faibles. \q Mais Dieu est comme un rocher qui soutient mon cœur. Il est tout ce qu’il me faut, pour toujours.

sw.L: Mwili wangu na moyo wangu vimedhoofika; \q mwamba wa moyo wangu na fungu langu [ni] Mungu milele.
sw.B: Ingawa mwili na moyo vinachakaa, \q Mungu ndiye mwamba ambao moyo wangu unategemea, na fungu langu milele.
sw.R: Mwili wangu na akili yangu vinaweza kudhoofika. \q Lakini Mungu ni kama mwamba unaoushikilia moyo wangu. Yeye ndiye ninayemhitaji milele.

decisions.choice: my portion: my share, all I have
decisions.reason: The word (cheleq) is a share of land. The priests had no land; God was their portion (Numbers 18:20; Psalm 16:5). So God is all the speaker owns.

decisions.choice: has failed: or may fail
decisions.reason: The verb is in the past tense: his body and heart are worn out, or even if they fail, God remains.

decisions.choice: the rock of my heart: the strength of my inner life
decisions.reason: God is the firm rock under him (18:3), holding up his heart when it fails.

source.text: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֣ה רְחֵקֶ֣יךָ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ הִ֝צְמַ֗תָּה כָּל־זוֹנֶ֥ה מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For look, those far from you will perish; you destroy everyone who acts as a prostitute from you.

en.L: For look, those far from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will perish; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} destroy everyone who strays from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in unfaithfulness.
en.B: Those who move far from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are lost; \q everyone who deserts {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to love another, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cut off.
en.R: People who stay far away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will die. \q You destroy everyone who turns away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to worship other gods.

fr.L: Car voici, ceux qui sont loin de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} périront ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détruis tous ceux qui s’écartent de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} par infidélité.
fr.B: Ceux qui s’éloignent de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} sont perdus ; \q tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}abandonnent pour en aimer un autre, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les retranches.
fr.R: Ceux qui restent loin de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} mourront. \q Tu détruis tous ceux qui se détournent de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} pour adorer d’autres dieux.

sw.L: Kwa maana tazama, walio mbali {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} wataangamia; \q {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unamwangamiza kila akuachaye {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} kwa kukosa uaminifu.
sw.B: Wale wanaojitenga mbali {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} wamepotea; \q kila anayekuacha {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ili kumpenda mwingine, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unamkatilia mbali.
sw.R: Watu wanaokaa mbali {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}} watakufa. \q Unamwangamiza kila mtu anayekuacha {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ili kuabudu miungu mingine.

decisions.choice: acts as a prostitute from you: is unfaithful to God
decisions.reason: The prophets picture Israel's turning to other gods as a wife's unfaithfulness to her husband (Hosea 1:2; Jeremiah 3:1).

decisions.choice: deserts you to love another (B); turns away from you to worship other gods (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of unfaithful love; Readable says what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: strays from you in unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the sense of the verb in words fit for public reading.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֤י׀קִֽרֲבַ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֗ים לִ֫י־ט֥וֹב שַׁתִּ֤י׀בַּאדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֣ה מַחְסִ֑י לְ֝סַפֵּ֗ר כָּל־מַלְאֲכוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I — [the] nearness of God for me [is] good; I have made in [the] Lord YHWH my refuge, to recount all your works.

en.L: But as for me, [the] nearness of God [is] good for me; \q I have made the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} my refuge, \q to recount all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works.
en.B: As for me, being close to God is my good; \q in the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} I have found my shelter, \q and I will tell of all {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done.
en.R: But for me, the best thing is to be close to God. \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} is where I go to be safe. \q I will tell everyone about all the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done.

fr.L: Mais moi, la proximité de Dieu [est] bonne pour moi ; \q j’ai fait du Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} mon refuge, \q pour raconter toutes {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} œuvres.
fr.B: Quant à moi, être près de Dieu, voilà mon bien ; \q c’est dans le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} que j’ai trouvé mon abri, \q et je raconterai tout ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait.
fr.R: Mais pour moi, le plus beau, c’est d’être près de Dieu. \q C’est auprès du Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} que je vais pour être en sécurité. \q Je raconterai à tous ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait.

sw.L: Lakini mimi, ukaribu wa Mungu [ni] mwema kwangu; \q nimemfanya Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} kuwa kimbilio langu, \q ili kusimulia kazi {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} zote.
sw.B: Lakini mimi, kuwa karibu na Mungu ndiyo mema yangu; \q kwa Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} nimepata kimbilio langu, \q nami nitasimulia yote uliyoyatenda {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}.
sw.R: Lakini kwangu, jambo bora kuliko yote ni kuwa karibu na Mungu. \q Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} ndiye ninayemkimbilia ili niwe salama. \q Nitamwambia kila mtu mambo yote uliyoyatenda {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}.

decisions.choice: the nearness of God is good: the psalm's answer
decisions.reason: The psalm began, "God is good to Israel" (verse 1); it ends with what that good is: to be near God. The "far from you" of verse 27 is its opposite.

decisions.choice: the Lord YHWH
decisions.reason: As in 71:5, the title followed by the divine name.

decisions.choice: your works: speaking to God again
decisions.reason: The verse speaks of God, then turns to him in the last words.
